forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38→0.15 (Judge, accepting DA). Observed transit rate May 20: ~2 commercial vessels/day against 50/day resolution threshold. Lloyd's war-risk premiums at 8–10% of hull against 1.5% indicator threshold — commercially prohibitive; a single Hormuz voyage costs $10–14M in insurance alone. IRGC 'coordinated passage' toll system announced May 20 creates an AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pathway per the forecast's own ambiguity rule. Iran's May 18 counter-proposal demanded reparations and zero nuclear concessions; Trump: 'totally unacceptable.' No signed MOU as of May 21. Hapag-Lloyd repeated 'not yet possible' May 20. Project Freedom paused May 6. 20-day remaining window intact but practically foreclosed absent a deal this week.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window, and the 7-day window is fully elapsed before EOD 2026-06-10. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. IRGC 'coordinated passage' toll system (announced May 20) vessels do NOT count and constitute AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO per this rule. Third-country vessels transiting under Iran's PGSA toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls. The 7-day window must be fully elapsed before EOD 2026-06-10.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition formally lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via formal dissolution bill passage OR no-confidence roll-call confirming sub-61 majority) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: WEEKLY CADENCE — p not adjusted (not Sunday; Codex DA #12 upheld). Observation update: On May 20, the Knesset passed a preliminary reading of a dissolution bill 110-0, with the coalition itself submitting the bill via whip Ofir Katz while Netanyahu was absent. Three additional full readings plus committee stage required before formal dissolution. No Knesset roll-call has confirmed majority loss on a confidence or budget vote. Smotrich has not formally departed. Functional coalition seat count approximately 60 — one below the 61-seat threshold. Judge logs for Sunday May 24 review. F5 at 0.40 is a subset path to F2 YES; aggregate probability of some elections-before-Oct-27 path estimated 0.55–0.60 at Sunday review.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if: (a) a Knesset roll-call vote on a formal no-confidence motion or budget confirms the coalition has lost its majority, OR (b) the Knesset dissolution bill passes all three readings and the House Committee sets an election date earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if the coalition maintains functioning majority through EOD Oct 27 and the mandatory election proceeds on schedule.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If dissolution bill passes all three readings but Netanyahu files legal challenge suspending enactment: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pending court ruling. If a coalition deal restores 61-seat majority and shelves dissolution: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU, or a signed MOU initiating structured negotiations) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25→0.20. Iran's May 18 counter-proposal (via Pakistan) demanded reparations, US troop withdrawal, end to blockade, sanctions removal, and zero nuclear concessions. Trump characterized proposal as 'totally unacceptable.' As of May 20, Trump told reporters sides are 'right on the borderline' and gave 'a few days.' Pakistan's interior minister made a second Tehran visit; Qatar-Pakistan bridging memo reportedly in circulation. Enrichment gap: Tehran's public floor 5 years; Washington's demand 20 years or HEU transfer. No Witkoff-Araghchi direct contact confirmed post-May-15. 15-day horizon technically intact but positions remain far apart.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US official (Witkoff, Kushner, or State Dept spokesperson) AND a named Iranian official (Araghchi, Gharibabadi, or MFA spokesperson) both publicly confirm a signed written framework or MOU — whether joint statement, separate statements citing the same document, or published MOU text. A signed MOU labeled 'ceasefire declaration' or 'letter of intent' that initiates a structured negotiation period also qualifies. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A ceasefire extension alone without a nuclear framework does NOT resolve YES.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; direct principal-level engagement removed Pakistani-channel lag in April. FLAG: confirm whether early-May Oman meeting is in the sourced record before next publish.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved NO at horizon. US State Department formally announced 45-day extension May 15-16, reaffirmed by spokesman Tommy Pigott. Lebanese government welcomed extension. No Beirut-governorate IDF airstrike detected May 19-21. No Hezbollah barrage above 50/day confirmed. IDF Chief Zamir's 'no ceasefire' framing describes operational posture in south Lebanon, not formal government withdrawal. Pentagon security track May 29; political talks June 2-3. All formal collapse criteria definitively excluded before EOD May 22.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse. Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date (via formal Knesset speech or final dissolution bill passage) before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22→0.40 (Judge between Analyst 0.35 and DA 0.45–0.55). On May 20, 110 of 120 MKs voted in favor of a preliminary dissolution reading — 110-0 — with the coalition itself submitting the bill via whip Ofir Katz while Netanyahu was absent. Three additional readings plus committee stage remain; no election date set. The June 1 horizon is 11 days away. Three readings in 11 days is procedurally feasible but not routine; House Committee has not committed to a compressed schedule. A Netanyahu-Haredi deal restoring 61-seat majority remains the primary scenario for shelving the bill; no such deal announced. 0.40 reflects the 110-0 vote as the strongest directional signal yet, with weight on procedural friction within the June 1 cutoff.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if: (a) Netanyahu delivers a formal Knesset speech naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27, OR (b) the Knesset dissolution bill passes its third and final reading and the House Committee formally sets an election date earlier than 2026-10-27, confirmed by official Knesset record before EOD 2026-06-01. NOTE: The May 20 preliminary dissolution reading (110-0) does NOT resolve YES — only third/final reading plus House Committee date-setting, or direct Netanyahu announcement, resolves.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal final Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Knesset preliminary dissolution reading does NOT resolve YES. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself, or a passed final dissolution vote, counts.

The 40-day June 30 horizon accommodates three remaining readings plus committee stage that the June 1 horizon (F5) does not. Primary scenario is passage given 110-0 coalition support; a Netanyahu-Haredi deal could shelve the bill. Initial p=0.65.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset plenum passes the third reading of the dissolution bill by simple majority and the House Committee sets an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if an alternative Knesset procedure achieves formal dissolution with election date earlier than 2026-10-27 confirmed by official Knesset record before EOD 2026-06-30. forecasts.question: Will the existing Iran-US ceasefire framework remain in effect (no resumed large-scale US/Israeli strikes on Iranian territory) through EOD 2026-06-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. The ceasefire has held since Operation Epic Fury's initial pause without a confirmed US or Israeli strike on Iranian territory. IDF and IRGC proxy combat continues across Lebanon, Gaza, and Yemen but without crossing the Iranian-territory threshold. Trump's 'few days' statement introduces diplomatic uncertainty, not military escalation per se — a talk collapse does not automatically restart strikes on Iranian territory given the acknowledged political costs. Initial p=0.62 reflects ceasefire durability offset by the 27-day horizon and the 'right on the borderline' diplomatic context.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the ceasefire holds through June 17 without confirmed resumption of US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory (CENTCOM or IDF confirming strikes on targets inside Iran's internationally recognized borders). NO if CENTCOM, IDF, or Pentagon formally confirms resumed strikes on Iranian territory before EOD June 17, OR if Iran's IRGC publicly confirms 'active war resumed.'
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM press releases or Pentagon press conference (primary). Reuters/AP/AFP quoting named US or Israeli military officials (secondary). Iranian IRGC or MoD official statement (corroborating).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: US strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen, IDF strikes in Lebanon/Gaza, or strikes on Iranian proxy positions in Syria or Iraq do NOT count unless CENTCOM explicitly characterizes them as part of resumed Operation Epic Fury. Cyber operations alone = NOT resolved. If Trump announces 'resuming strikes' but no physical strike occurs within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO after 72h window.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US publicly confirm they have agreed on the duration of an Iranian uranium enrichment moratorium (any named figure accepted by both sides) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Iran's public floor is 5 years; Washington's demand is 20 years or HEU transfer — a 15-year gap on the specific parameter this forecast tracks. No Witkoff-Araghchi direct meeting confirmed post-May-15. Iran's reparations demand on the table means nuclear enrichment is not yet the primary negotiating item. Initial p=0.15.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US official (Witkoff, Kushner, or State Dept spokesperson) AND a named Iranian official (Araghchi, Gharibabadi, or MFA spokesperson) both publicly confirm agreement on the same enrichment moratorium duration — whether in a joint statement, separate statements citing the same figure, or a published MOU text. NO if both parties are still publicly citing different figures at EOD June 5, or if talks collapse. A 'significant progress' statement without a named duration does NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP both quoting named principals from both sides citing the same duration. OR official State Department + Iran MFA simultaneous statements. A single-source claim with no Iranian confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Iran agrees on a figure but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If agreement is on a range rather than a specific duration = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless both sides confirm the range is the agreed landing zone.
